newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch 1997 manufacturing investment seen up 22 pct.
newsitem.headline: Dutch 1997 manufacturing investment seen up 22 pct.

text.p: Dutch manufacturers expect their investment in fixed assets to rise by 22 percent in guilder terms next year compared with 1996, the Central Bureau of Statistics (CBS) said on Monday.
The CBS said the strong growth in planned investment was due largely to a surge in projected capital spending in the petroleum- and coal-processing industries.
If big projects in these sectors were excluded, then planned investment by manufacturers would show a four percent increase in guilder terms in 1997, it added.
The CBS figures are based on its end-of-year survey of business investment. The figures are not adjusted to take account of inflation and include leased plant and equipment.
For these reasons the figures differ from those used by the CBS in its quarterly and annual national accounts for the Netherlands, the CBS said.
